lesson_title: S3: The Infinite Hard Drive in the Sky

ava_lesson_intro.ava_speaks: CS1B · S3: The Infinite Hard Drive in the Sky. Ren teaching mode on.

lines: S3: The Infinite Hard Drive in the Sky

blocks.ava_speaks: Awesome. EC2-ல compute (brain) எப்படி work ஆகுது-னு பாத்துட்டோம். But ஒரு app-க்கு photos, videos, user uploads-லாம் எங்க store பண்றது? That brings us to Pillar 2: Amazon S3.
blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: S3 stands for 'Simple Storage Service'. EC2 வந்து renting a computer by the hour-னா, S3 is literally renting an infinite hard drive in the sky.

board_actions.text: The infinite hard drive in the sky
Used for files, images, videos, backups

whiteboard_data.heading: Pillar 2: Amazon S3
points: S3 = Simple Storage Service
The infinite hard drive in the sky
Used for files, images, videos, backups

blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: Normally, நம்ம laptop-ல folders குள்ள folders-னு வைப்போம். This is a nested hierarchy. 1000 files இருந்தா இது ஓகே. But Swiggy or Zomato-ல millions of food photos இருக்கும். Folder structure use பண்ணா, file தேடி எடுக்குறதுக்குள்ள search ரொம்ப slow ஆகிடும்.
blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: So, S3 completely removes folders. Instead, it uses 'Buckets'. Think of a Bucket as a massive, flat container. You just drop your files directly into this giant Bucket. No messy mazes, no endless clicks.

board_actions.text: Everything lives in a giant, flat Bucket.
Buckets must have globally unique names.

whiteboard_data.heading: Buckets, not Folders
points: No deep, messy folder hierarchies.
Everything lives in a giant, flat Bucket.
Buckets must have globally unique names.

blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: And S3-ல அத 'files'-னு சொல்ல மாட்டோம், 'Objects'-னு சொல்லுவோம். Object = Your File + Metadata (Nametags). அந்த Nametags-ல file-ஓட details இருக்கும். அதனால தான் Hotstar-ல billions of videos இருந்தாலும், instant-ஆ scale ஆகி play ஆகுது.

whiteboard_data.heading: What is an Object?
points: Object = File + Metadata (Nametags)
Instantly searchable at scale.
Perfect for massive media libraries.

blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: Best part? S3 storage is literally infinite. Hard drive 'full' ஆகுமோ-னு கவலையே வேணாம். And it's incredibly safe. AWS physically copies your data across multiple data centers. Uncrashable storage.

board_actions.text: Pay only for exactly what you store.
11 9s of Durability (data loss is near impossible).

whiteboard_data.heading: Infinite & Uncrashable
points: Unlimited storage capacity.
Pay only for exactly what you store.
11 9s of Durability (data loss is near impossible).

blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: So, EC2 is the brain, S3 is the infinite bucket for files. Clear-ஆ? You are now ready to configure this service in the real terminal.
blocks.speaker: Ren

workspace_tasks.question: Myntra needs to securely store 50 million high-resolution product photos. When users open the app, these images must load instantly across India. Which AWS storage architecture is the correct choice?
options: Save the photos directly on the local hard drives of their EC2 web servers to keep them close to the application.
Create a complex, 10-level deep folder hierarchy in an on-premise server to keep the categories organized.
Store them in an Amazon S3 Bucket as Objects for infinite, flat scalability and fast retrieval.
Store the raw image files inside a Relational Database (RDS) to keep them strictly organized.
workspace_tasks.ava_feedback_correct: S3 infinite storage. Photos, videos, user uploads- S3 Bucket- Object- store doing correct architecture. EC2 hard drive-, server crash photos- (Data loss).
workspace_tasks.ava_feedback_wrong: S3 infinite storage. Photos, videos, user uploads- S3 Bucket- Object- store doing correct architecture. EC2 hard drive-, server crash photos- (Data loss).
workspace_tasks.explanation: S3 infinite storage. Photos, videos, user uploads- S3 Bucket- Object- store doing correct architecture. EC2 hard drive-, server crash photos- (Data loss).

workspace_tasks.question: CampusKart stores 8 million product photos in one S3 bucket. Support asks: 'How do we find every image tagged season=festive without walking nested laptop-style folders?' What property of an S3 Object makes that possible?
options: Each Object is actually a tiny EC2 that runs search code.
Each Object is the file plus Metadata (nametags) — so season=festive can be attached and queried without deep folder mazes.
S3 only stores zip archives, so support must unzip locally.
S3 forces the same nested C:\Users\... folder tree as a laptop, so metadata isn't needed.
workspace_tasks.ava_feedback_correct: Object = File + Metadata. nametags billions of photos- instant retrieve — laptop folder maze.
workspace_tasks.ava_feedback_wrong: S3 Object = file + metadata nametags. That's how CampusKart finds festive SKUs without folder archaeology.
workspace_tasks.explanation: Object = File + Metadata. nametags billions of photos- instant retrieve — laptop folder maze.
